title: Representative Ciscomani concludes August district work period across Arizona's 6th District
text:
Representative Ciscomani concludes August district work period across Arizona’s 6th District
J. E. Carter
Representative Juan Ciscomani concluded a district work period in August, traveling nearly 2,500 miles throughout Arizona’s 6th Congressional District to attend 50 in-person events with constituents, local businesses, and community organizations. According to a Sep. 2 announcement, Ciscomani used the time to meet with local leaders and highlight millions of dollars in federal investments he has helped secure for the district.
Ciscomani said, "Getting out into the district and hearing directly from the people I represent is one of the most important parts of my job. From healthcare providers and veterans to educators, small business owners, law enforcement, and families, these conversations give me a firsthand understanding of what our communities need. I am taking these perspectives back to Washington to continue fighting for real solutions that make a difference right here in Southern Arizona." The congressman participated in meetings, roundtables, site visits and focused on $42.7 million in preliminary federal funding advocated for through 20 Community Project Funding requests as part of Fiscal Year 2027 appropriations bills.
Projects highlighted included $6.76 million for Eloy’s Frontier Street Mill & Overlay Project; $4.2 million for Oro Valley Police Department technology; $3 million for Marana’s Interstate 10 interchange improvements; $2 million for Benson Hospital expansion; $2.7 million for Pima JTED career education programs; among others related to public safety and infrastructure.
Ciscomani also met with healthcare leaders at facilities such as Pima Heart & Vascular and Benson Hospital to discuss challenges facing patients and providers in rural areas. He visited Chiricahua Community Health Center regarding expanding care access in underserved communities.
Veterans’ issues were another focus during meetings with his Veterans Advisory Council, where he provided updates on veteran-related legislation shaped by constituent input. At an award ceremony held in Sierra Vista—the first there—19 veterans were honored along with one civilian supporter.
Education initiatives included visiting Pima JTED alongside Small Business Administration Deputy Administrator Bill Briggs to highlight federal funding supporting Innovation Tech High School programs like construction technology and bioscience. He also attended educator recognition events and met students receiving scholarships from the Lapan Sunshine Foundation.
Business engagement activities featured attendance at the SPARK Business Summit hosted by Marana Chamber of Commerce and Better Business Bureau of Southern Arizona as well as welcoming new businesses like Dickey’s Barbecue Pit to Marana. Ciscomani hosted Speaker Mike Johnson and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent at PepsiCo Casa Grande facility for discussions on manufacturing policy impacts such as tax cuts encouraging investment.
Faith leaders across the district discussed affordable housing needs, public safety concerns, and support for faith-based organizations serving families during separate meetings with Ciscomani, who also attended a Tucson naturalization ceremony where he shared his experience becoming a U.S. citizen twenty years ago.
The congressman ended his August schedule participating in local high school football game ceremonies while being recognized by BridgeGrades as both Arizona's most bipartisan congressional member this term—and among Congress's top twenty overall—citing commitment to working across party lines,according to Representative Juan Ciscomani's office.
Juan Ciscomani is currently serving in Congress representing Arizona’s 6th District after replacing Ann Kirkpatrick beginning January 2023. In previous elections against Kirsten Engel—in both 2022 (winning by just over one percentage point) and again more recently—he secured victories. Born in Hermosillo, Mexico in 1982 before moving later to Tucson where he now lives, he graduated from University of Arizona with a Bachelor of Arts degree.according to Representative Juan Ciscomani's office.
